lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.33 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops students’ ability to connect spoken language with written text. It helps them build confidence in reading along with audio support.
Look for careful listening, accurate recognition of key vocabulary including new words, and appropriate intonation when reading aloud.
“Oh no, my eyes have turned into grapes and my mouth is a banana. What would your face look like if it was made of fruit? What would you use for your eyes?.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.33 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers develops reading comprehension by guiding students to focus on key details in short sentences. This activity helps them read carefully and select the answer that best matches the information.
Look for correct answer choices, neat bookwork and good comprehension.
“Now my nose has become a pear! Quick,  help me answer these questions before someone starts eating part of my face!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.115 - A Look and say the sounds

details: Look and say the sounds introduces the target phoneme by helping students connect each picture with its beginning sound. This activity supports early phonics awareness and accurate sound production.
Look for careful reading, clear pronunciation of the target sound, and students identifying the correct picture–sound match.
“To turn my face back to normal, I need to know what sounds these letters make! Please say them for me!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Match strengthens sound–picture connections by guiding students to draw a line from each picture to the correct letter. This activity practises accuracy and reinforces letter sound recognition.
Look for accurate lines linked to the correct letter, neat bookwork, and students checking the initial sound before completing the task.

Trace helps students practise letter formation and spelling by guiding them to follow the outline of each word carefully.
Look for accurate tracing, correct letter shapes, careful pencil control, and correct spelling.
“That’s my eyes back! To get my nose, I need you to write these words.. Which one matches each picture?”

Write develops independent writing accuracy by having students reproduce the word in boxes without outlines.
Look for neat writing, correct spelling, and careful attention to sizing so letters fit in the boxes.

lessonPlan.topic: p.117 - A Find and colour the words with d

details: Find and colour the words with d helps students practise letter recognition and reading accuracy by identifying words that contain the target letter ‘d’ in a group of words.
Look for correct selection of words with ‘d’, careful colouring, and students checking each word.
“Make me a smile by helping these children cross the river!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Write words develops independent writing and spelling accuracy by guiding students to complete words with the first letter given.
Look for correct spelling, neat handwriting and consistent letter sizing within the lines.
